_notes.lr: 4e-3 at batch 512 IS the reference configuration exactly (it used 8 TPU replicas x 64 = 512 global, lr 5e-4 x 8). Keep the lr/batch ratio if you change either.
_notes.num_layers: Number of (3x Conv1DBlock + TransformerBlock) STAGES. 2 = reference base model at dim 192; the reference's '4x' variant is 4 stages at dim 384.
_notes.grad_clip: 1.0. The reference leaves this off (its clipvalue=1 is commented out) and 0.0 is what run 1787483814 used — it diverged at the exact step AWP switched on (epoch 15: train loss 2.01 -> 5.79 = ln(250), val acc 0.746 -> 0.017, stem weight norm 16 -> 224, never recovered). AWP takes its step from a gradient measured at an adversarially perturbed point, which is exactly where an unclipped update is most dangerous. Set back to 0 only to reproduce that failure.
_notes.awp_delta: The reference author reports NaN loss roughly 1 run in 5 at 0.2; 0.1 is the documented fallback. 0 disables AWP entirely and halves epoch time. If a run still diverges at awp_start_epoch with grad_clip on, drop this to 0.1 before touching anything else.
_notes.es_patience: 30 epochs without a val-acc gain > es_min_delta ends the run. Generous on purpose: a one-cycle cosine makes real gains late, while the LR anneals, so a short patience would cut the run's best phase. Set to the epoch cap to disable.
_notes.collapse_ratio: The fast guard, and the reason it exists: run 1787483814 spent 285 of its 300 epochs training a model that had already died. Val accuracy below this fraction of the run's own best, for collapse_patience consecutive epochs, ends the run. 0 disables it.
_notes.collapse_patience: 3 consecutive epochs, so a single bad epoch never trips it.
_notes.stop_after_epoch: 0 = disabled. Ends the run after N epochs WITHOUT changing the cosine schedule, which stays laid out over `epochs` - lowering `epochs` instead would compress the one-cycle and put epoch 15 at 15% of peak LR, a different experiment. Used by the notebook's S5b switch-ablation.
_notes.weight_decay: Decoupled. torch applies lr*wd*p and tfa applies (lr*0.1)*p, so 0.1 here reproduces the reference exactly.
_notes.diff_mode: 'forward' = reference (dx[t]=x[t+1]-x[t], reads 2 frames ahead). 'backward' = causal/streaming-safe. Changing it invalidates comparability with the reference number.
_notes.batch_size: 512, chosen by measurement on this machine (RTX 4080 Super 16GB, i7-14700K): 300 epochs takes 8.86h at w=0, 1.39h at w=8, peak 7.9GB. 256 is SLOWER overall (6.31h) despite a cheaper step, because it doubles the step count and the per-step cost is dominated by fixed overhead. 1024 is much worse (12.85h) and peaks at 15.7GB, near the card limit.
_notes.num_workers: 8, measured. The dataloader was ~85% of the step: batch 512 goes from 640ms/step at w=0 to 101ms at w=8. Beyond 8 it flattens and very slightly regresses (w=12 104ms, w=16/20 106ms), so 8 is the knee. Requires the lazy per-process cache open in features.FirstPlaceDataset - holding the 3GB array as an attribute makes Windows spawn pickle it to every worker and fail with OSError 22.
_notes.precision: fp16 + GradScaler. bf16 was measured at 105ms/step vs fp16's 104ms - no speed difference on Ada - so fp16 stays. Switch to bf16 only if AWP produces NaN losses, since bf16 has fp32 range and cannot overflow.
_notes.pin_memory: Deliberately OFF and must stay off. A padded batch at 512 is ~557MB, so pinning across 8 workers x prefetch exhausts page-locked host memory and raises 'CUDA error: out of memory' from the pin thread.
_notes.torch_compile: Not available here: torch.compile raises TritonMissing on Windows (no Triton wheel). Do not spend time on it - it was the main remaining GPU-side lever.
